verdict.line: You lose when you trade into full Fury or get caught dismounted; you win by poking him down before level 6 and cashing in the surprise R engage.

brief.thesis: Kled's E (Jousting) dash-and-return and W (Violent Tendencies) attack-speed burst let him out-trade Renekton in short exchanges before Renekton's Fury bar fills, but once Renekton crosses 50 Fury his Q (Cull the Meek) and W (Ruthless Predator) both upgrade into bigger damage, a shield-destroying triple slash, and a 1.5s stun. The 51.9% win rate over 104 games and Kled's listed lane and solo-kill advantage both assume you fight him low-Fury and stay mounted — that edge evaporates the moment either condition flips.

theirWindow.what: His Q (Cull the Meek) heals and hits harder, and his W (Ruthless Predator) becomes a 3-hit shield-destroying stun at 1.5s instead of 0.75s. Disengage and let the cooldown reset rather than trading into it.

yourWindow.what: Dash in with E (13s cooldown at rank 1), auto, dash back out through him for the second hit, and layer W's four-attack speed burst on top. This is your best damage window before his Fury scaling and his R (Dominus, 120s cooldown at rank 1) come online.

start.why: The 53% win rate start over 90.6% of games — the extra AD and sustain keep you even in the auto-trading war before your dash tools are online.

boots.why: Picked in 84.5% of games for a 55.1% win rate; flat reduction on Renekton's auto-reliant Q and W poke matters more than magic resist here.

playing.title: Track the Fury bar, not just HP
playing.detail: Renekton's Q and W both get stronger past 50 Fury. If you see his Fury creeping up from autos, back off and wait for it to decay instead of trading into the upgraded W stun.

playing.title: Dash-return before level 6
playing.detail: Use E (Jousting) to dash in, auto, then recast to dash back through him. This is your highest-value trading tool while his all-in is still just Q into W.

playing.title: Cash in R at level 6
playing.detail: OP.GG's own data flags using Chaaaaaaaarge!!! the moment it's up at level 6 for a surprise kill — his flash and ignite usage spike around when you first threaten this.

playing.title: Never extended-trade while dismounted
playing.detail: Dismounted, your Q becomes Pocket Pistol (a knockback poke, not a hook), and you deal less champion damage. Disengage and let Skaarl's courage refill from minions before re-engaging.

playing.title: Pop W before he can stun through it
playing.detail: Violent Tendencies' four-attack burst is strongest thrown out before Renekton's W (0.75s stun at low Fury, 1.5s above 50) can interrupt your attack string.

playing.title: Respect his E dash range
playing.detail: Slice and Dice has 450 range and can be recast for a bonus-damage, armor-shredding return hit — don't stand at the edge of trade range expecting him to not reach you.

playing.title: Freeze if you're ahead post-8
playing.detail: Once Renekton's Fury scaling and his 120s-cooldown R start covering his all-in windows, play the wave rather than force fights — your lane edge is front-loaded.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, win rates, and pick rates above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning — why these windows exist, when to fight, when to back off — is my own read of the ability kits, not OP.GG's.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid fighting Renekton when he has his Fury full or when you unmounted Skaarl. Try to use Chaaaaaaaarge!!![R] upon reaching level 6 to get a surprise kill.
